### Sources

The daily source program screened five previously untracked candidate families: **Alice & Books**, **Loyal Books**, **Planet eBook**, **ManyBooks**, and **Better Gutenberg**. At least three received source-specific audits beyond initial discovery.

1. **Alice & Books / AliceAndBooks — admitted as the passing integration.** First-party library and representative work pages describe the reviewed classics as U.S. public-domain/open-license reading routes and expose ordinary reader PDF/EPUB/online-reading options. The site's current Terms of Use separately prohibit automated/non-human access and systematic extraction for a database/directory. WebNR therefore admitted only a manually bounded `Alice & Books Public Domain Discovery Starter`: the official library plus `Pride and Prejudice`, `Frankenstein`, and `White Nights`, represented by explicit first-party destination URLs and WebNR-authored labels/descriptions. It performs no crawl, synchronization, API use, metadata copy, mirror, background polling, credential use, or access-control bypass. This is discovery-only because of source-access terms, not because the underlying reviewed works lack public-domain evidence.
2. **Loyal Books — audited and deferred for richer text integration.** Its first-party material emphasizes public-domain audiobooks and says much of its material derives from Project Gutenberg and LibriVox, while the ebook layer overlaps heavily with sources WebNR already maintains. This cycle did not establish a source-specific machine interface or item-level provenance advantage that would justify another synchronized text catalog. It remains a candidate rather than a manufactured duplicate integration.
3. **Planet eBook — audited and deferred.** First-party work pages describe publication from Australia and explicitly tell readers to check copyright status in their own jurisdiction. WebNR does not collapse that jurisdiction-specific statement into a blanket worldwide public-domain ingestion claim. No incremental reader/runtime value over existing maintained public-domain routes justified an integration today.
4. **ManyBooks — audited and deferred as a blanket source.** Its first-party description shows an ecosystem that began with Project Gutenberg material and now also includes self-publishing authors, free/promotional books, and account-mediated downloads. A future integration would need item-level rights/provenance and account/access boundaries rather than treating the entire platform as one license class.
5. **Better Gutenberg — screened for follow-up.** It reformats public-domain material into modern EPUBs and overlaps substantially with the already maintained Project Gutenberg/GITenberg routes. A later audit should prove incremental reader value plus format, attribution, update, and bulk-access boundaries before admission.

The new Alice & Books starter became the **24th maintained source family**. Rotating health review also rechecked Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, and GITenberg at their existing capability boundaries; no reproducible failure required removal or downgrade.
